cards.text: Amos, a shepherd from Tekoa, is carrying the LORD's word to Israel (Amos 1:1). Now he turns to the distinguished ones of the foremost nation in Zion and on Mount Samaria, the people the house of Israel comes to. And friend, he does NOT open with "Good morning."

cards.question: Amos says woe to the distinguished ones in Zion and on Mount Samaria. How are they living?

cards.text: Then Amos sends them on a trip. Cross over to Calneh, go on to great Hamath, then down to Gath of the Philistines, and take a good look.

cards.question: After sending them to Calneh, Hamath and Gath, Amos asks if Israel is better than whom?

cards.text: Next, Amos says they dismiss the day of calamity. That's hitting snooze on a smoke alarm.

cards.question: These folks dismiss the day of calamity. True or false: That keeps a reign of violence far away from them.

cards.text: Now Amos walks right into their house. Beds inlaid with ivory, couches for lounging. IVORY, friend. I spent years sleeping on a takeout menu.

cards.question: Lounging on their ivory beds and couches, what are these folks dining on?

cards.text: After dinner, the music starts. They improvise songs on the harp like David, Israel's great king.

cards.question: Besides playing the harp like David, true or false: These folks invent their own musical instruments.

cards.text: They drink wine by the bowlful. Not the cup, friend, the BOWL, and then they anoint themselves with the finest oils.

cards.question: With all that wine and oil, Amos says they fail to ___ over the ruin of Joseph.

cards.text: Then Amos says, "Therefore." When a prophet says therefore, friend, you put the cookie DOWN.

cards.question: Amos says their feasting and lounging will come to an end. Where are these distinguished ones headed?

answers.text: Into exile as the first captives
To the palace as honored guests
Into battle as the first soldiers

cards.text: Then the Lord GOD swears by Himself, and He speaks about Jacob, the people of Israel. When God swears by Himself, nobody in the room is checking their phone.

cards.question: The LORD swears there's something in Jacob He abhors. He abhors Jacob's ___ and detests his citadels.
The LORD says He will deliver up the city. True or false: Everything inside the city will be spared.

cards.text: Then it gets heavy. If ten men are left in one house, they too will die.
A relative comes to burn the bodies. As he picks them up to carry them out, he calls to someone inside the house.

cards.question: The relative carrying out the bodies asks the one inside if anyone else is with him. What's the answer?
The relative answers with "Silence," and a warning. True or false: He warns them to call on the name of the LORD.

cards.text: For the LORD gives a command about two houses. The great house and the small house.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD's command spares the small house while the great house is smashed to pieces.

cards.text: Then the LORD asks, "Do horses gallop on the cliffs? Does one plow the sea with oxen?" That's like stamping cookies on the ceiling, friend.

cards.question: Horses on cliffs and oxen plowing the sea just don't fit. What does the LORD say Israel has done that doesn't fit either?

cards.text: And they're celebrating. They rejoice in Lo-debar and talk about taking Karnaim.

cards.question: The people of Israel talk about taking Karnaim. How do they say they did it?

cards.text: Then the LORD, the God of Hosts, says, "For behold." And He's talking straight to the house of Israel.

cards.question: The LORD says He will raise up a ___ against the house of Israel to oppress them.

cards.text: That nation will oppress them from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of the Arabah. And that's how the LORD, the God of Hosts, ends this word.

findings.problem: The right answer 'These kingdoms' is the only answer that is a kingdom or place. The wrong answers 'Their own fathers' and 'The prophets of old' are groups of people, not the same kind of thing, so the right answer stands out. The card before it just named three kingdoms. The wrong answers should be other kingdoms or nations that are real Bible details.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: 'After dinner, the music starts' adds an order in time. Amos 6:4-5 lists the dining and the songs with no time between them.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: 'and then they anoint themselves' adds an order. Amos 6:6 says 'You drink wine by the bowlful and anoint yourselves' and gives no sequence.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: 'the ruin of Joseph' is the first mention of Joseph, and no card says who or what Joseph means here. A baker may think it means Joseph the man and not his descendants among Israel's tribes.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The right answer 'None' is one word. The wrong answers 'Just one more' and 'Two are hiding' are three words each, so the right answer stands out by its length.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: 'He warns them' uses 'them' without saying who it is. The question gives no context for it. Amos 6:10 has the relative speaking to the one person inside, so 'them' also gets the text wrong.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
